assertion: voted 2-1 on Thursday, November 5, to approve a permanent 3.55% residential rate increase for Public Service Company of Oklahoma customers
why_not: The fetched passage supports the grade: it says the 3.55% is only what PSO told OCC staff, staff must still review it, and the order is formally an Interim Order, so 'permanent' is wrong; the vote and the 3.55% as a reported figure are right.
independent_value: Vote 2-1 on Nov 5 confirmed (Hiett, Bingman yes; David no). Order No. 761871 is formally an Interim Order; 3.55% is an unconfirmed figure and not an addition to current bills.

assertion: Since July 1, 2026, residential customers have been paying an interim charge of approximately $11 per month while regulators considered the company's rate request.
Under the final order, those temporary collections will not be refunded to residential customers, although certain large industrial customers are expected to receive credits.
independent_value: PSO and Chair David say residential no refund, industrial refunds; order requires refunds with interest within 90 days; OCC said it could not yet confirm eligibility. Order is interim.

assertion: PSO has six days to submit revised tariffs and detailed financial calculations following the commission's decision.
independent_value: Order requires updated accounting and revised class cost study within six calendar days; revised tariffs follow after an objection period.

assertion: The approved 3.55% residential rate increase will begin appearing on customer bills during the December 2026 billing cycle.
independent_value: PSO says December billing cycle; order applies new rates from first regular cycle after tariffs are approved.

assertion: A new large-load tariff is intended to ensure that high-demand customers pay for infrastructure and electrical system improvements required to serve their operations.
independent_value: Tulsa Flyer: all commissioners approved a large-load tariff (>75 MW class) but its regulation, including bring-your-own-generation, is unresolved; other coverage says PSO's proposed tariff may be considered in 2027.

assertion: The provision follows Oklahoma's Data Center Customer Ratepayer Protection Act, which establishes safeguards designed to prevent costs associated with major new electricity users from being shifted unfairly onto existing residential and small-business customers.
reason: The cited oksenate.gov page returned HTTP 307 and could not be read; Tulsa Flyer reports a 2026 law requiring separate terms for large customers such as data centers, consistent with the claim, but the act's name and text were not verified.
measure: electricity retail rates Oklahoma utility average price residential

assertion: Although the percentage increase has been finalized, the precise dollar impact on an average residential electricity bill has not yet been released.
independent_value: The percentage is not finalized: the order is interim and OCC staff must review PSO's numbers before confirming impacts. The dollar-impact half is true.
